resale_co.name: Certificate of Approval for Occupancy (Change of Occupancy, Sale)
resale_co.issued_by: Division of Housing & Landlord Compliance (Housing Inspection & Landlord Compliance Office)
requirements: Working smoke detectors not more than 10 years old; battery-only units must have 10 year sealed batteries, and hardwired units need battery backup
Working carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of all sleeping rooms
Portable fire extinguisher (at least 1A:10B:C, no more than 10 pounds) mounted in or within 10 feet of the kitchen (checklist dated April 2026)
Walls, ceilings, floors and bathroom tiles in good repair; bathroom doors lock
Working hot and cold water with shut off valves, secured toilets, approved drain traps
Stove and oven work and ranges have an anti-tilt bracket
GFCI outlets within 6 feet of water (bathroom, kitchen, unfinished basement); no extension cords in place of wiring
Water heater and boiler in good order; relief valve discharge pipe 2 to 6 inches from the floor; gas shut off valve on each gas appliance
Roof and structure sound; chimneys safe; fireplaces and wood stoves need a Level II chimney certification
No double-keyed deadbolts on exit doors; no keyed bedroom locks; windows open, lock and have screens
Handrails and guards on stairs, porches and decks; fences and pool barriers in good repair
House numbers at least 3 inches high, visible from the curb; grass cut, no rodents or insects
Sump pumps discharge outside and not into the sanitary sewer
Work done without permits must be permitted and inspected, and open construction permits must be closed
Well and septic systems must be approved by the Health Department

fees.label: Certificate of Approval for Occupancy, sale of a single family property

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Change of Occupancy Application Portal, or fill out the Certificate of Approval for Occupancy Sale Application for Single Family Property and submit it to the Office of Housing Inspections, 2090 Greenwood Avenue, Room 302, Hamilton. Only the owner, the owner's realtor, the owner's attorney or a power of attorney may apply. Pay by cash, credit card or check. Inspections are scheduled in a morning (9:30 to noon) or afternoon (1:00 to 3:30) window.

resale_co.notes: Hamilton Township requires a certificate of approval from the Office of Housing Inspections before any change in occupancy, and posts a separate sale application for a single family property ($200.00, April 2025 form). No sale application or fee for a two-family home was found; the Township also posts a separate rental application. The Township code (ecode360 HA0682) could not be opened, so lead time, validity and reinspection fees were not confirmed. The email HousingHT@HamiltonNJ.com is decoded from the email protection link on the Housing page; the sale application prints it as housinght@hamiltonnj.com. Office hours on the Housing page: Mon, Wed, Fri 8:30 AM-4:15PM; Tues and Thurs 8:30 AM-2:30 PM. The Township website sometimes shows a bot check ('Just a moment') to repeated automated requests; the checklist PDF was read through a normal fetch when curl was challenged. Rental properties built before 1978 also need a lead certification (not a sale requirement).

requirements: Smoke detectors not more than 10 years old; battery-only units must have 10 year sealed batteries; hardwired units need replaceable or 10 year sealed battery backup
Carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of all sleeping rooms
The April 2026 Change of Occupancy Checklist still lists a portable fire extinguisher (at least 1A:10B:C, no more than 10 pounds) mounted in or within 10 feet of the kitchen

authorities.name: Hamilton Township Division of Housing & Landlord Compliance (smoke detector compliance for the Township fire code agency)
authorities.how_to_apply: For owner-occupied 1 and 2 family homes the smoke, carbon monoxide and fire extinguisher items are checked in the Housing change of occupancy inspection (see the Change of Occupancy Checklist). No separate smoke certificate application or fee is posted. Apply for the Certificate of Approval for Occupancy through the Housing office or its online portal and ask whether the smoke and CO certificate is issued with it.

evidence.quote: Smoke detectors: All dwelling units are required to be equipped with working smoke detectors. Smoke detectors shall not be more than 10 years old.
Fire Extinguishers: Every single & two family dwelling unit must be provided with a portable fire extinguisher
The Fire Prevention Bureau is charged with inspecting all of the building and structures in the Township, with the exception of owner occupied one and two-family dwellings, at least once a year.

fire_cert.notes: The July 2026 state registry lists Hamilton Township (municipality, code M) as a single fire code enforcing agency; no separate fire districts are listed (the Township site has a 'Fire District Consolidation' page, and fire service now runs through the Township Fire Division). The state directory names the Township Housing Department as the smoke detector compliance office, and the Fire Prevention Bureau page says the Bureau does not inspect owner occupied one and two-family dwellings. The Fire Official is Scott McCormick (Fire Official/Fire Protection Subcode Official, 609-586-4194 extension 1052, SMcCormick@HamiltonNJ.com decoded from the email protection link on the Fire Prevention Bureau page; the state directory lists (609) 890-6927 and smccormick@hamiltonfirenj.org). The directory's smoke detector compliance phone (609) 890-3666 is the Township inspections (construction) number; the Housing page lists 609-890-3665. Search summaries quoted an ordinance with a $50 certificate of smoke detector compliance fee from a 'Bureau of Fire Prevention in the Township of Hamilton', but it could not be tied to this Hamilton (Hamilton Township in Atlantic County also uses ecode360) and was not used.

other_items.label: Open construction permits
other_items.detail: Open construction permits must be closed before the Certificate of Occupancy can be issued; work done without permits must be permitted and inspected.

other_items.label: Well and septic
other_items.detail: Well and septic systems must be approved by the Health Department before the certificate is issued.

other_items.label: Fireplaces and wood stoves
other_items.detail: A Level II certification from a qualified chimney sweep company is required for fireplaces and wood burning stoves.
